In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

antimicrobial agents should only be prescribed when absolutely necessary, and that the duration of therapy should be limited to that required to eradicate the infection, and not be extended in order to prevent relapse.
the impact of antimicrobics on the intestinal microflora varies greatly with the agent used, the dosage and the route of administration, and the duration of treatment.
antimicrobial agents should be administered as short a course as possible, and that they should be administered in such a way as to minimise their impact on the normal microflorae.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antimicrobials affect the normal microfloral ecosystem in the gastrointestinal tract in a dose-dependent way.
antimicrobials should only be used when strictly necessary, and for a limited period.
antimicrobial therapy should be used only when absolutely necessary, and that antimicrobials should be used in the most effective way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of antimicrobial agents should be based on the clinical indication and the risk of ecological disturbance should be taken into consideration when choosing the antimicrobial agent.
the use of antimicrobics in humans should be limited as much as possible, and the use of broad spectrum antimicrobials should be avoided.
antimicrobials are not the only agents that may disturb the microflora.
